diagnoses.summary: High Hotelling T2 and SPE with dominant contribution from CSTR pressure measurement and strong PCV-related signals indicate a H2 PCV issue propagating coherently through the circuit. Likely PCV-related fault causing elevated reactor pressure and compensatory responses.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations and the plant has a failed Bottoms pump train (BOTTOMS) accompanied by a trip (P203_TRIP). The most likely root cause is a Bottoms pump trip causing loss of bottoms flow, with secondary contributors related to H2 PCV or sensor bias providing lesser evidence.
PCA shows a high SPE with coherent T² movement; most evidence points to a degraded or stuck H2 PCV (vent valve) affecting reactor pressure through the CSTR vent system.

The PCA shows a large, coherent upset dominated by CSTR pressure measurement with strong SPE indicating a PCV (H2 purge) related fault affecting reactor pressure control. The rule-based hypotheses point to H2 PCV issues, especially capacity degradation or stuck closed, with sensor bias as a secondary possibility.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset dominated by reactor pressure indicating a H2 purge valve (PCV) issue propagating through the system, with the strongest rule-based hints pointing to H2 PCV problems.

High SPE with a dominant contribution from the CSTR pressure measurement and H2 PCV control signals points to an H2 PCV related fault (actuator) affecting reactor pressure management, rather than a purely sensor drift or a process upset.

Both Hotelling T² and SPE are violated with a strong dominant contribution from reactor pressure. PCV-related actuator faults at the CSTR vent valve best explain a coherent process upset propagating through the system, consistent with the top contributors.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous spike in reactor pressure and elevated SPE, dominated by CSTR pressure measurement. The most plausible faults are related to the H2 PCV (vent) being degraded or stuck, causing high reactor pressure and forcing the PID to compensate in a way that matches the observed signals.
PCA shows a large, coherent upset with strong reactor pressure signal; likely issues are related to the H2 PCV (valve)—capacity degradation or being stuck—potentially with a sensor bias contributing.

High SPE with coherent T² movement suggests a process upset affecting pressure correlations, likely tied to the H2 PCV or a pressure sensor fault. The dominant SPE contributor is meas.cstr_pressure_bar, pointing to PCV-related issues or a biased pressure sensor.
Abnormal PCA with coherent upset driving reactor pressure high; most likely H2 PCV related fault causing elevated reactor pressure and abnormal cstr_pressure readings.

High SPE with a single dominant contributor to SPE (meas.cstr_pressure_bar) and no active alarms or saturated loops; coherent up-move in T2 but a broken correlation pattern suggests a sensor fault is driving the abnormal PCA signal, with possible upstream actuator faults affecting pressure dynamics.

High T² and high SPE with dominant rise in CSTR pressure signal indicate a coherent upset dominated by the H2 vent (PCV) system, most consistent with PCV actuator degradation or stuck condition affecting reactor pressure. Sensor bias in the reactor pressure sensor could also contribute but is less likely to be the primary cause.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violated, dominated by a rise in reactor pressure and related control action. The fixed-rule hypotheses point to H2 PCV issues as the primary driver, with secondary plant-feed/outlet constraints possible.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with both T2 and SPE violated, dominated by a reactor-side holdup/load upset and influent/outlet capacity issues at the CSTR, with possible PCV/controller/pressure sensor involvement.

Both Hotelling T² and SPE are violated with a coherent plant upset; multiple strong contributors point to a condenser cooling issue propagating through the column, with secondary indications of CSTR outlet capacity issues and possible liquid leaks. The most likely fault is condenser cooling loss, with secondary faults in CSTR outlet capacity loss and CSTR liquid leak.

Abnormal PCA is indicating a large, coherent upset with high move along normal correlations and strong SPE, dominated by the reflux/condenser area signals. The most likely immediate issues are condenser cooling loss or reflux flow issues causing the column to experience abnormal heat removal and associated tray temperatures; sensor anomalies are less favored given high SPE but TOP_TIC contributions point to reflux-side disturbances. A secondary possibility is CSTR outlet capacity loss or liquid leaks contributing to holdup shifts.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violated, with strongest evidence pointing to condenser-side heat removal loss causing the column to run hot and shift compositions toward acetone-rich streams. This is consistent with elevated tray/top temperatures and rising column pressure, and is supported by multiple high-contribution measurements.

PCA flags a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations. Distillate acetone abnormal with distillation indicators and elevated top temperatures point to a condenser cooling effectiveness issue propagating through the column, likely in combination with a saturated CSTR outlet loop.

PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with strong distillation column symptoms and an alarm on the distillate acetone composition. The most consistent fault is condenser cooling effectiveness loss affecting the column balance, with secondary contributions from RB_LIC being out of range and possible reflux flow issues.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with both T2 and SPE violations, with the strongest evidence pointing to a condenser-related issue propagating through the column (likely condenser cooling loss) causing elevated distillate acetone deviation and column pressure behavior.

PCA flags a strong, coherent process upset with substantial disturbance in distillation product composition and tray temperatures, plus an active DISTILLATE acetone alarm. Most likely a condenser cooling/equipment issue causing reduced condenser effectiveness and abnormal distillate composition, with secondary suspicion of reboiler/reflux control limits being challenged.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong SPE (sensor correlations largely preserved but with a significant cause), with the top contributors pointing to the distillation section and condenser interaction. The active alarm DIST_X_L and a saturated RB_LIC point to a condenser-related issue driving the distillate composition anomaly and column pressure dynamics.
